# local 0014: A volatile right operand of an assignment is read again for each use of the value of the assignment

- Category: [Fixes](../../fix.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17228
- Recommended action: Apply the patch. It does not fix two other mcs51 faults with volatile objects, which local 0018 and local 0019 describe.
- Patch: [local-0014.patch](../../patches/local-0014.patch), commit [`d3171240f`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/d3171240f8d80ff9fa60c0855234bcfb9e3554fa). Apply after `bugs-4157-1.patch`, `bugs-3121.patch`, `bugs-3847.patch`, `bugs-3849.patch`, `local-0013.patch`.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

C11 6.7.3 requires that an expression that refers to a volatile object is evaluated strictly
according to the rules of the abstract machine, which evaluates the right operand of an assignment
once. When the right operand is a volatile object and the value of the assignment is used, the
code that SDCC generates reads the object once for the assignment and once more for each use of
the value. Some hardware registers return another value at the second read, and some clear a flag
at each read. The file below was compiled with `sdcc -mmcs51 --model-large -S vol.c` on r17228.

```c
#include <stdint.h>

__sfr __at (0x90) P1;
__sfr __at (0xa0) P2;
uint8_t g8;
void use8 (uint8_t);

void sfr_v (void) { g8 = P2 = P1; }
void sfr_cond (void) { uint8_t x; if ((x = P1) & 0x80) use8 (x); }
```

Both functions have two instructions that read `P1`. `sfr_v` has `mov _P2,_P1` and then
`mov a,_P1` for the store to `g8`. `sfr_cond` stores the value of one read in `x` and tests bit 7
of the value of a second read. With the patch, each function has one instruction that reads `P1`.

More functions were compiled to assembly for mcs51, stm8, and z80, on r17200 with the earlier
patches of this report. The object is read again for integers of 8, 16, and 32 bits, for `float`,
and for pointers, when the left operand is volatile, a local variable, or an object that is
accessed through a pointer. With `--model-large`, the code for mcs51 reads a volatile object in
xdata once, and it reads `__sfr` and `__sfr16` objects and objects in `__data`, `__idata`, and
`__pdata` again. Two cases are correct on the three ports: a right operand that is accessed
through a pointer variable, and a global left operand that is not volatile.

## Cause

`geniCodeAssign` in `src/SDCCicode.c` returns the right operand as the value of the assignment.
For an object outside far space, `geniCodeRValue` returns the operand of the symbol and does not
generate a read to an iTemp, so each iCode that uses the value reads the object. For an object in
far space, `geniCodeRValue` generates the read to an iTemp, and the object is read once. For a
global left operand that is not volatile, `geniCodeAssign` copies the right operand to an iTemp,
and a comment at that code refers to bug #1369874.

## Fix

In `ast2iCode` in `src/SDCCicode.c`, the case of `=` generates an iCode that copies a volatile
right operand that is not an iTemp to a new iTemp, and it passes the new iTemp to
`geniCodeAssign`. The copy is not made when the left operand is a bit-field or a bit, for which
`geniCodeAssign` returns the left operand. It is also not made for an assignment that is a
statement, so that the code of assignment statements does not change. The static pointer
`unusedValue` points to the tree whose value is not used. The handler of `NULLOP` and `BLOCK` sets
it for each of the two subtrees, and the case `LABEL` sets it for the statement of the label. An
assignment whose value is not used gets the copy when it is an operand of a comma operator or of
a cast to `void`.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/assignment-volatile.c` has two functions. `testValue` has 14 assertions
on the values of assignments with a volatile right operand, for every port. `testReadOnce` has 23
assertions and counts reads for stm8, where the suite has the simulator interface of ucsim at the
memory address 0x7fff. Each read of the interface gives the next byte of an answer, so the byte
that the test reads after an expression shows how many times the expression read an object at
that address. Without the patch, on r17228 with the earlier patches of this report, 19 of the 37
assertions fail for stm8, and the 14 assertions pass for mcs51-small and mcs51-large.

With the patches of this report on r17228, the regression suite has 0 failures for host, stm8,
ucz80, and six mcs51 variants: the four models, and `--stack-auto` with the small and large
models. The diagnostics suite has 0 failures for mcs51, mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80, and
stm8. On the nine regression targets, the size of every other test is equal with and without the
patch. The other ports were not built.

For mcs51 the suite stops ucsim at a read of the interface, and for ucz80 the interface is in the
output address space, so the test does not count reads for them. For mcs51, a program that is not
part of the patch counts the reads of an `__sfr`, an `__sfr16`, and an `__sfr32` in ucsim, with
the interface at SFR address 0xf8. It was run on r17200 with the earlier patches of this report.
Without the patch, each of its expressions whose value is used reads the object twice with
`--model-large`, with and without `--stack-auto`, and `i = vl = SIF` stores the first byte of the
answer in the volatile `vl` and the second byte in `i`. With the patch, each expression reads the
object once for the four models and for the large model with `--stack-auto`.

## Related

- The patch for local 0013 precedes this patch in `ast2iCode`. With that patch alone, a volatile
  right operand is read once when the types of the two operands differ in signedness only.
- The entries local 0018 and local 0019 describe two faults of mcs51 that are present with and
  without the patch. `genCast` reads the most significant byte of a volatile signed object twice,
  and `ptrPseudoSymSafe` does not test for `volatile`. With the patch, `g8 = w8 = st.m8` reads a
  volatile member `m8` in near data twice for mcs51-small, which is the fault of local 0019.
